newsitem.title: USA: Standard Pacific sells thrift unit.
newsitem.headline: Standard Pacific sells thrift unit.

text.p: Standard Pacific Corp said the company entered into a definitive stock purchase agreement to sell the federally chartered thrift subsidiary, Standard Pacific Savings, FA to First Alliance Corp.
The agreement provides the purchase price will be the adjusted stockholder's equity of savings as of the closing date, plus $575,000.

Consummation of the deal is tentatively scheduled to occur on or before September 30, but is contingent upon approval of the transaction by the Office of Thrift Supervision and certain other conditions.
As of March 31, shareholders' equity of Standard Pacific Savings was $21 million. Assets of Standard Pacific Savings were $254 million.
